other_names.value: avian chlamydiosis (name used for the infection in birds)

value: parrots, parakeets, cockatiels, budgerigars, pigeons, turkeys, chickens, ducks and other birds
inhaling dust from dried droppings or respiratory secretions of infected birds
among birds via droppings, and also via feathers and eggs
occasionally by bites or beak-to-mouth contact
infection can also show no obvious signs at all

incubation_period.value: 5 to 14 days in humans, though symptoms can start later

diagnosis.value: in birds, confirmed with antigen/antibody testing or PCR; false negatives are possible so clinical signs and lab tests are used together

value: do not stack cages directly on top of each other
clean cages and food/water containers regularly
wash hands after handling birds or cage items
wet surfaces before cleaning instead of dry sweeping or vacuuming
wear gloves and a mask when handling infected birds or cleaning cages

treatment_overview.value: in people, antibiotics are the standard treatment and starting them early leads to better outcomes

summary.value: Psittacosis is a bacterial infection carried by birds, including chickens, ducks and turkeys, that can spread to people who breathe in dust from infected droppings, causing flu-like illness or pneumonia. Sick birds may show eye and breathing problems or watery droppings, but many show nothing at all, and good hygiene and cage cleaning are the main ways to prevent it since there is no vaccine.
